capsule.title: CommonJS can't require() an ES module (ERR_REQUIRE_ESM): load it with dynamic import()

problem.symptom: Error [ERR_REQUIRE_ESM]: require() of ES Module ./lib.mjs not supported
problem.description: A CommonJS file loads an ESM-only module with require(). Older Node versions reject it. Dynamic import() works from CommonJS on every supported Node version.

applicability.notes: Since Node 22.12 / 20.19, require() of synchronous ESM works, so the problem itself may not reproduce there.

limitations.proves: main.cjs prints the ESM export when loaded with this runtime.
limitations.does_not_prove: Behavior with packages that use top-level await or conditional exports.

capsule.author: cafe-curator

capsule.title: __dirname is not defined in ES modules: use import.meta.dirname

problem.symptom: ReferenceError: __dirname is not defined in ES module scope
problem.description: CommonJS globals (__dirname, __filename) do not exist in .mjs files. Node 20.11+ provides import.meta.dirname.

applicability.notes: For older Node use fileURLToPath(new URL('.', import.meta.url)).

limitations.proves: main.mjs prints its own directory.
limitations.does_not_prove: Bundler behavior (webpack/esbuild may rewrite import.meta).

capsule.author: cafe-curator

detect.note: Also applies to .js files when package.json has "type": "module".

capsule.title: Node type stripping rejects TypeScript parameter properties: declare fields explicitly

problem.symptom: SyntaxError [ERR_UNSUPPORTED_TYPESCRIPT_SYNTAX]: TypeScript parameter property is not supported in strip-only mode
problem.description: Running .ts files directly with Node (type stripping, default since 22.18) only erases types. Syntax that needs code generation, like constructor(public x), fails. Declare fields and assign them.

applicability.notes: Bun and tsc support parameter properties; the problem is specific to Node's strip-only mode.

limitations.proves: point.ts runs and computes the sum with this runtime's TypeScript handling.
limitations.does_not_prove: Other strip-only restrictions (enums, namespaces) or tsc type errors.

capsule.author: cafe-curator

detect.note: Only matters if you run .ts files directly with Node (type stripping); tsc and bundlers accept it.

capsule.title: Node type stripping needs explicit .ts extensions in imports

problem.symptom: Error [ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND]: Cannot find module './util' imported from main.ts
problem.description: When Node runs TypeScript directly, ESM resolution does not guess extensions. Import './util.ts' (and enable allowImportingTsExtensions in tsconfig for type checking).

limitations.proves: main.ts imports util.ts and runs with this runtime.
limitations.does_not_prove: That tsc accepts the import without allowImportingTsExtensions.

capsule.author: cafe-curator

capsule.title: Import assertions (assert { type: 'json' }) were removed in Node 22: use import attributes (with)

problem.description: Node 22 dropped the old import-assertions syntax. JSON modules now use import attributes: import data from './data.json' with { type: 'json' }.

files.main.mjs:
import data from "./data.json" assert { type: "json" };
console.log(data.name);

import data from "./data.json" with { type: "json" };
console.log(data.name);

limitations.proves: The JSON module loads with this runtime.
limitations.does_not_prove: TypeScript or bundler support for the with syntax.

capsule.author: cafe-curator

capsule.title: (OLD FIX) Importing JSON in ESM: add assert { type: 'json' }

problem.symptom: TypeError: Module "./data.json" needs an import attribute of "type: json"
problem.description: ESM refuses to import JSON without declaring its type. This capsule records the fix that was common in 2022-2023 (import assertions).

applicability.notes: Claim as originally written; kept to show how evidence detects regressions.

files.main.mjs:
import data from "./data.json" assert { type: "json" };
console.log(data.name);

limitations.proves: The JSON module loads with this runtime.
limitations.does_not_prove: Anything about newer Node versions; see superseding capsule.

capsule.author: cafe-curator

capsule.title: Importing JSON in ESM: add with { type: 'json' } (import attributes)

problem.symptom: TypeError: Module "./data.json" needs an import attribute of "type: json"
problem.description: ESM refuses to import JSON without declaring its type. Current syntax: import attributes with `with`.

files.main.mjs:
import data from "./data.json" with { type: "json" };
console.log(data.name);

limitations.proves: The JSON module loads with this runtime.
limitations.does_not_prove: TypeScript or bundler support.

capsule.author: cafe-curator

capsule.title: Top-level await is not allowed in CommonJS: wrap it in an async function

problem.symptom: SyntaxError: await is only valid in async functions and the top level bodies of modules
problem.description: A .cjs (or CommonJS .js) file uses await at the top level. Either convert the file to ESM or wrap the code in an async IIFE.

limitations.proves: main.cjs prints the awaited value.
limitations.does_not_prove: Error handling of the wrapped promise (unhandled rejections).

capsule.author: cafe-curator

capsule.title: JSON deep copy turns Dates into strings: use structuredClone

problem.symptom: TypeError: copy.createdAt.getTime is not a function
problem.description: JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(obj)) loses Dates, Maps, undefined and more. structuredClone (Node 17+) keeps them.

limitations.proves: Dates and Maps survive the copy.
limitations.does_not_prove: Behavior with functions or class instances (structuredClone drops prototypes).

capsule.author: cafe-curator

capsule.title: Array.prototype.sort mutates the input: use toSorted for a sorted copy

problem.symptom: The caller's array changed order after calling a helper that 'returns a sorted list'
problem.description: sort() sorts in place and returns the same array. toSorted() (Node 20+) returns a new array.

limitations.proves: The result is sorted and the input is untouched.
limitations.does_not_prove: Sort stability or performance on large arrays.

capsule.author: cafe-curator

capsule.title: Summing prices with floats gives 0.30000000000000004: add integer cents

problem.description: Binary floating point cannot represent 0.1 exactly. Convert to integer minor units before adding.

limitations.proves: Two-decimal totals are exact for these inputs.
limitations.does_not_prove: Currency rounding rules, amounts above 2^53 cents, or more than 2 decimals.

capsule.author: cafe-curator

capsule.title: JSON.stringify throws on BigInt: serialize it as a string

problem.symptom: TypeError: Do not know how to serialize a BigInt
problem.description: JSON has no BigInt type. Use a replacer that converts bigint values to strings (and parse them back explicitly).

files.lib.cjs: module.exports.toJson = (o) => JSON.stringify(o, (_k, v) => (typeof v === "bigint" ? v.toString() : v));

limitations.proves: BigInt values serialize as exact decimal strings.
limitations.does_not_prove: That consumers parse them back as BigInt.

capsule.author: cafe-curator

capsule.title: datetime.fromisoformat rejects a trailing 'Z' before Python 3.11: normalize it to +00:00

problem.description: Before Python 3.11, fromisoformat only accepted its own output format. Replacing a trailing Z with +00:00 works on all versions.

applicability.notes: On 3.11+ the original code already works.

files.check.py:
from parse import parse

d = parse("2026-11-24T15:17:00Z")
assert d.utcoffset().total_seconds() == 0, d
assert (d.hour, d.minute) == (15, 17), d

limitations.proves: A Z-suffixed timestamp parses as UTC.
limitations.does_not_prove: Other ISO 8601 variants (week dates, fractional hours) on old Pythons.

capsule.author: cafe-curator

detect.note: Only a problem for strings ending in 'Z' before Python 3.11.

capsule.title: datetime.utcnow() is deprecated and naive: use datetime.now(timezone.utc)

problem.symptom: DeprecationWarning: datetime.datetime.utcnow() is deprecated and scheduled for removal
problem.description: utcnow() returns a naive datetime and is deprecated since Python 3.12. datetime.now(timezone.utc) returns an aware UTC datetime.

files.check.py:
import warnings

warnings.simplefilter("error", DeprecationWarning)
from clock import now_utc

d = now_utc()
assert d.tzinfo is not None and d.utcoffset().total_seconds() == 0, d

limitations.proves: now_utc returns an aware UTC datetime without deprecation warnings.
limitations.does_not_prove: Callers that compare it with naive datetimes (they will now raise TypeError).

capsule.author: cafe-curator

capsule.title: distutils was removed in Python 3.12: stop using distutils.version.LooseVersion

problem.description: PEP 632 removed distutils in 3.12. For simple dotted versions, compare tuples of ints; for real version specs use the packaging library.

files.check.py:
from ver import newer

assert newer("1.10", "1.9")
assert not newer("1.2", "1.10")

limitations.proves: Numeric dotted versions compare correctly.
limitations.does_not_prove: Pre-releases (1.0rc1), epochs or local versions: use packaging.version for those.

capsule.author: cafe-curator

detect.note: Hidden when setuptools is installed in the same environment (it ships a distutils shim).

capsule.title: CSV header starts with \ufeff (BOM from Excel): open with encoding='utf-8-sig'

problem.description: Files saved by Excel and some Windows tools start with a UTF-8 byte order mark. utf-8-sig strips it.

files.check.py:
from reader import header

assert header("data.csv") == ["name", "price"], header("data.csv")

limitations.proves: The BOM is not part of the first header.
limitations.does_not_prove: Files in other encodings (cp1252, UTF-16).

capsule.author: cafe-curator

capsule.title: Mutable default argument keeps state between calls: default to None

problem.description: Default values are evaluated once. A list default is shared by every call.

files.check.py:
from bag import add

assert add(1) == [1]
assert add(2) == [2]
shared = [0]
assert add(3, shared) == [0, 3]

limitations.proves: Each call without a bucket starts empty; passing a list still appends to it.
limitations.does_not_prove: Anything about other mutable defaults (dicts, sets) elsewhere in the code.

capsule.author: cafe-curator

capsule.title: str.lstrip('abc_') strips characters, not a prefix: use removeprefix

problem.description: lstrip treats its argument as a set of characters. Python 3.9+ has str.removeprefix for prefixes.

files.check.py:
from names import strip_prefix

assert strip_prefix("abc_cab") == "cab"
assert strip_prefix("abc_x") == "x"
assert strip_prefix("zzz") == "zzz"

limitations.proves: Only the exact prefix is removed.
limitations.does_not_prove: Case-insensitive prefixes.

capsule.author: cafe-curator

capsule.title: f-string SQL lets input rewrite the query: use parameter placeholders

problem.description: Interpolating user input into SQL allows injection. sqlite3 placeholders (?) pass values separately from the query.

files.users.py:
def find(conn, name):
    return conn.execute(f"SELECT name FROM users WHERE name = '{name}'").fetchall()

def find(conn, name):
    return conn.execute("SELECT name FROM users WHERE name = ?", (name,)).fetchall()

files.check.py:
import sqlite3
from users import find

conn = sqlite3.connect(":memory:")
conn.execute("CREATE TABLE users (name TEXT)")
conn.executemany("INSERT INTO users VALUES (?)", [("ann",), ("bob",)])
assert find(conn, "ann") == [("ann",)]
assert find(conn, "x' OR '1'='1") == []
assert find(conn, "o'brien") == []

limitations.proves: These inputs cannot change the query.
limitations.does_not_prove: Injection elsewhere (dynamic table/column names cannot use placeholders).

capsule.author: cafe-curator

capsule.title: datetime.fromtimestamp(0) depends on the machine's time zone: pass tz=timezone.utc

problem.symptom: Epoch printed as 1969-12-31T21:00:00 on a server in Buenos Aires
problem.description: Without tz, fromtimestamp converts to local time. Results change with the TZ of the machine.

files.check.py:
from epoch import epoch_iso

assert epoch_iso().startswith("1970-01-01T00:00:00"), epoch_iso()

limitations.proves: The epoch is rendered in UTC regardless of TZ.
limitations.does_not_prove: Correct behavior for timestamps before 1970 on Windows.

capsule.author: cafe-curator

detect.note: Calls without tz= depend on the machine's time zone.

capsule.title: (OLD FIX) Detect PNG files regardless of extension with imghdr.what

problem.symptom: A PNG saved as photo.dat is not recognized as an image
problem.description: Checking file extensions misses misnamed files. This capsule records the classic stdlib answer: imghdr.

applicability.notes: Claim as originally written; kept to show regression detection.

files.detect.py:
def kind(path):
    return "png" if path.endswith(".png") else None

files.check.py:
from detect import kind

with open("photo.dat", "wb") as f:
    f.write(b"\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n" + b"\x00" * 24)
assert kind("photo.dat") == "png", kind("photo.dat")

limitations.proves: A PNG header is detected without relying on the extension.
limitations.does_not_prove: Support in newer Pythons (imghdr was removed in 3.13 by PEP 594).

capsule.author: cafe-curator

capsule.title: Detect PNG files by their magic bytes (imghdr is gone in Python 3.13)

problem.description: PEP 594 removed imghdr in Python 3.13. For a single format, compare the 8-byte PNG signature; for many formats use a maintained library.

files.detect.py:
def kind(path):
    return "png" if path.endswith(".png") else None

PNG = b"\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n"


def kind(path):
    with open(path, "rb") as f:
        return "png" if f.read(8) == PNG else None

files.check.py:
from detect import kind

with open("photo.dat", "wb") as f:
    f.write(b"\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n" + b"\x00" * 24)
with open("notes.png", "wb") as f:
    f.write(b"just text")
assert kind("photo.dat") == "png", kind("photo.dat")
assert kind("notes.png") is None, kind("notes.png")

limitations.proves: PNG content is detected by signature and a fake .png is rejected.
limitations.does_not_prove: Detection of other formats or truncated files.

capsule.author: cafe-curator

capsule.title: A failing command in a pipeline is ignored: set -eo pipefail

problem.symptom: The deploy script printed 'deployed' and exited 0 although a step failed
problem.description: By default a pipeline's status is the last command's. pipefail propagates failures; -e stops the script.

files.run.sh:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -eo pipefail
false | true
echo "deployed"

files.check.sh:
out=$(bash run.sh 2>&1)
code=$?
if [ "$code" -eq 0 ]; then echo "failure was swallowed"; exit 1; fi
case "$out" in *deployed*) echo "continued after failure"; exit 1 ;; esac
exit 0

limitations.proves: A failure inside a pipeline stops the script with a non-zero status.
limitations.does_not_prove: Behavior of commands inside if/while conditions, where -e does not apply.

capsule.author: cafe-curator

capsule.title: read mangles backslashes and leading spaces: use IFS= read -r

problem.symptom: C:\Users\fer became C:Usersfer and indentation disappeared
problem.description: Without -r, read treats backslashes as escapes; without IFS=, it trims leading and trailing whitespace.

files.print.sh:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
while read line; do
  echo "$line"
done < paths.txt

#!/usr/bin/env bash
while IFS= read -r line; do
  echo "$line"
done < paths.txt

files.check.sh:
if [ "$(bash print.sh)" != "$(cat paths.txt)" ]; then
  echo "output differs from input"
  exit 1
fi

limitations.proves: Lines are reproduced byte for byte (for this input).
limitations.does_not_prove: Handling of a last line without a trailing newline.

capsule.author: cafe-curator

capsule.title: imghdr was removed in Python 3.13: detect PNG by its magic bytes

problem.description: PEP 594 removed imghdr in 3.13. For a single format, compare the 8-byte signature; for many formats use a maintained library (e.g. filetype, Pillow).

files.detect.py:
PNG = b"\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n"


def kind(path):
    with open(path, "rb") as f:
        return "png" if f.read(8) == PNG else None

files.check.py:
from detect import kind

with open("photo.dat", "wb") as f:
    f.write(b"\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n" + b"\x00" * 24)
with open("notes.png", "wb") as f:
    f.write(b"just text, not an image")
assert kind("photo.dat") == "png", kind("photo.dat")
assert kind("notes.png") is None, kind("notes.png")

limitations.proves: PNG content is recognized by signature and a text file named .png is rejected.
limitations.does_not_prove: Detection of formats other than PNG (imghdr knew ~15).

capsule.author: cafe-curator

capsule.title: pipes was removed in Python 3.13: use shlex.quote

problem.description: pipes.quote was an alias of shlex.quote; the module is gone in 3.13 (PEP 594).

files.check.py:
from shell import cmd

assert cmd('a b.txt') == "cat 'a b.txt'", cmd('a b.txt')
assert cmd("it's") == "cat 'it'\"'\"'s'", cmd("it's")
assert cmd('plain') == 'cat plain'

limitations.proves: Paths with spaces and quotes are quoted exactly as before.
limitations.does_not_prove: Use of pipes.Template (no stdlib replacement; use subprocess pipelines).

capsule.author: cafe-curator

capsule.title: cgi was removed in Python 3.13: parse Content-Type with email.message

problem.description: cgi.parse_header is gone in 3.13 (PEP 594). email.message.Message parses header parameters the same way.

files.check.py:
from headers import content_type

assert content_type('text/html; charset=utf-8') == ('text/html', {'charset': 'utf-8'}), content_type('text/html; charset=utf-8')
assert content_type('application/json') == ('application/json', {})
assert content_type('multipart/form-data; boundary="x y"') == ('multipart/form-data', {'boundary': 'x y'})

limitations.proves: Media type and parameters (including quoted ones) parse as cgi.parse_header did.
limitations.does_not_prove: Replacements for cgi.FieldStorage (use a web framework or multipart parser).

capsule.author: cafe-curator

capsule.title: unittest.makeSuite was removed in Python 3.13: use TestLoader().loadTestsFromTestCase

problem.description: makeSuite, findTestCases and getTestCaseNames were deprecated in 3.11 and removed in 3.13.

files.check.py:
import unittest
from suite import suite

s = suite()
assert s.countTestCases() == 2, s.countTestCases()
r = unittest.TextTestRunner(stream=open('/dev/null', 'w')).run(s)
assert r.wasSuccessful()

limitations.proves: The suite is built with the same tests and runs.
limitations.does_not_prove: Custom prefix/sortUsing arguments of makeSuite (set them on the TestLoader).

capsule.author: cafe-curator

capsule.title: typing.io / typing.re were removed in Python 3.13: import IO, Pattern from typing

problem.description: The typing.io and typing.re pseudo-submodules warned since 3.8 and are gone in 3.13.

files.check.py:
import typing
from types_ import name

with open('x.txt', 'w') as f:
    assert name(f) == 'x.txt'
assert name.__annotations__['f'] is typing.IO

limitations.proves: The annotation resolves to typing.IO and the function works.
limitations.does_not_prove: Third-party stubs that still reference typing.io.

capsule.author: cafe-curator

capsule.title: uu was removed in Python 3.13: use binascii.b2a_uu

problem.description: uu is gone in 3.13 (PEP 594). binascii implements the same line encoding.

files.check.py:
import binascii
from uuenc import encode

data = bytes(range(256)) * 2
out = encode(data, 'blob.bin')
lines = out.split(b'\n')
assert lines[0] == b'begin 644 blob.bin', lines[0]
assert out.endswith(b'end\n')
body = [l for l in lines[1:] if l not in (b'', b' ', b'end')]
assert b''.join(binascii.a2b_uu(l) for l in body) == data

limitations.proves: Output round-trips byte-exact and keeps the begin/end framing.
limitations.does_not_prove: uu.decode replacements (use binascii.a2b_uu per line).

capsule.author: cafe-curator

capsule.title: imp was removed in Python 3.12: load modules with importlib.util

problem.description: The imp module, deprecated since 3.4, is gone in 3.12. importlib.util.spec_from_file_location replaces load_source.

files.plugins.py:
import importlib.util
import sys


def load(path):
    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location('plugin', path)
    mod = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    sys.modules['plugin'] = mod
    spec.loader.exec_module(mod)
    return mod

files.check.py:
import os
from plugins import load

os.makedirs('p', exist_ok=True)
with open('p/plug.py', 'w') as f:
    f.write('VALUE = 41 + 1\n')
m = load('p/plug.py')
assert m.VALUE == 42, m.VALUE

limitations.proves: A module is loaded from an arbitrary path and executed.
limitations.does_not_prove: Other imp functions (find_module, reload: use importlib.reload).

capsule.author: cafe-curator

capsule.title: assertEquals and other unittest aliases were removed in Python 3.12: use assertEqual

problem.description: Deprecated camelCase aliases (assertEquals, assertNotEquals, assertRegexpMatches, failUnless, ...) are gone in 3.12; tests error out.

files.check.py:
from legacy_tests import run

assert run() is True

limitations.proves: The test runs and passes with the current method names.
limitations.does_not_prove: That the assertion itself is meaningful.

capsule.author: cafe-curator

capsule.title: configparser.SafeConfigParser was removed in Python 3.12: use ConfigParser

problem.description: SafeConfigParser was an alias of ConfigParser since 3.2 and is gone in 3.12.

files.check.py:
from conf import port

assert port('[server]
port = 8080
') == 8080
assert port('[DEFAULT]
port = 1
[server]
') == 1

limitations.proves: Values and DEFAULT inheritance work the same.
limitations.does_not_prove: readfp() (also removed: use read_file).

capsule.author: cafe-curator

capsule.title: ssl.wrap_socket was removed in Python 3.12: use an SSLContext

problem.description: The module-level ssl.wrap_socket is gone in 3.12. Build an SSLContext; this capsule keeps the OLD default (no certificate verification) on purpose so behavior does not change silently. Turn verification on for real clients.

files.check.py:
import socket
import ssl
from tls import client

a, b = socket.socketpair()
s = client(a)
assert isinstance(s, ssl.SSLSocket)
assert s.context.verify_mode == ssl.CERT_NONE
s.close(); b.close()

limitations.proves: A client TLS socket is created with the same (unverified) defaults.
limitations.does_not_prove: That skipping verification is safe for your use (it usually is not).

capsule.author: cafe-curator

capsule.title: locale.format was removed in Python 3.12: use locale.format_string

problem.description: locale.format (deprecated since 3.7) is gone in 3.12.

files.check.py:
import locale
from money import fmt

locale.setlocale(locale.LC_ALL, 'C')
assert fmt(1234567) == '1234567', fmt(1234567)
assert fmt(-5) == '-5'

limitations.proves: Formatting output is identical under the C locale.
limitations.does_not_prove: Output under other locales (same function, so it should match).

capsule.author: cafe-curator

capsule.title: inspect.getargspec was removed in Python 3.11: use getfullargspec or signature

problem.description: getargspec (deprecated since 3.0) is gone in 3.11.

files.check.py:
from intro import params


def f(a, b=2, *rest, **kw):
    pass


assert params(f) == ['a', 'b'], params(f)
assert params(lambda: 0) == []

limitations.proves: Positional parameter names match getargspec's.
limitations.does_not_prove: Keyword-only parameters (getargspec refused them; getfullargspec reports them separately).

capsule.author: cafe-curator

capsule.title: @asyncio.coroutine was removed in Python 3.11: use async def

problem.description: Generator-based coroutines were removed in 3.11.

files.jobs.py:
import asyncio


async def double(x):
    await asyncio.sleep(0)
    return x * 2

files.check.py:
import asyncio
from jobs import double


async def main():
    return await asyncio.gather(double(1), double(21))


assert asyncio.run(main()) == [2, 42]

limitations.proves: The coroutine is awaitable and returns the same values.
limitations.does_not_prove: Code that relied on generator methods (send/throw) of the old coroutine.

capsule.author: cafe-curator

capsule.title: util.isBoolean/isString/... were removed in Node 23+: use typeof and Array.isArray

problem.symptom: TypeError: util.isBoolean is not a function
problem.description: The deprecated util.is* type checks (except isArray) were removed in Node 23, so Node 24 LTS breaks code that still calls them.

files.types.cjs:
const util = require('node:util');
exports.kind = (v) => (util.isBoolean(v) ? 'bool' : util.isString(v) ? 'str' : util.isNullOrUndefined(v) ? 'none' : 'other');
exports.kind = (v) => (typeof v === 'boolean' ? 'bool' : typeof v === 'string' ? 'str' : v === null || v === undefined ? 'none' : 'other');

limitations.proves: Same classification for booleans, strings, null/undefined and others.
limitations.does_not_prove: util.isDate/isRegExp/isError replacements (use instanceof or util.types).

capsule.author: cafe-curator

capsule.title: util.log was removed in Node 23+: log with console.log and your own timestamp

problem.symptom: TypeError: util.log is not a function
problem.description: util.log was deprecated and removed in Node 23.

limitations.proves: The message is printed with a time of day, like util.log did.
limitations.does_not_prove: The exact util.log timestamp format.

capsule.author: cafe-curator

capsule.title: Dirent.path was removed in Node 24: use dirent.parentPath (Node >= 20.12)

problem.symptom: TypeError [ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE]: The "path" argument must be of type string. Received undefined
problem.description: fs.Dirent#path was an alias of parentPath; it is undefined in Node 24, so path.join(d.path, d.name) throws. parentPath only exists since Node 20.12/21.4.

limitations.proves: Full paths of directory entries are built correctly.
limitations.does_not_prove: Recursive readdir behavior.

capsule.author: cafe-curator

capsule.title: zlib bytesRead was removed in Node 24: use bytesWritten

problem.symptom: Compression stats are NaN/undefined: zlib stream bytesRead is undefined
problem.description: The misnamed zlib bytesRead property (deprecated since Node 10) is undefined in Node 24; bytesWritten has the same value.

const zlib = require('node:zlib');
exports.gzipStats = (buf) => new Promise((res) => { const z = zlib.createGzip(); const out = []; z.on('data', (c) => out.push(c)); z.on('end', () => res({ input: z.bytesRead, output: Buffer.concat(out).length })); z.end(buf); });

const assert = require('node:assert');
require('./gz.cjs').gzipStats(Buffer.alloc(5000, 'a')).then((s) => { assert.strictEqual(s.input, 5000); assert.ok(s.output > 0 && s.output < 5000); }).catch((e) => { console.error(e.message); process.exit(1); });

limitations.proves: The number of input bytes is reported correctly.

capsule.title: crypto.createCipher was removed in Node 22: use createCipheriv with a real key and IV

problem.symptom: TypeError: crypto.createCipher is not a function
problem.description: createCipher derived keys insecurely (MD5, no salt) and was removed in Node 22. Old ciphertexts need the legacy EVP_BytesToKey derivation to decrypt; new data should use scrypt + random IV.

limitations.proves: Round trip works, ciphertexts are randomized, and a wrong password fails.
limitations.does_not_prove: Decrypting data produced by the old createCipher (needs EVP_BytesToKey; not included).
